name: Positive 4-3-3 DM Wide

slots.why: Keeps the role simple but must distribute securely into the short build-up when the press allows it.
Support full-back provides width and a safe build-up option without vacating the back line too aggressively.

Ball-playing defender who takes the goalkeeper's short kicks and starts Play Out Of Defence, finding the holding midfielder or the DLP(S). The short build-up needs one passer at the back, so this slot is fixed.
Central defender on the right, the safer partner beside the ball-playing defender. Cover is the alternate.
Support full-back provides width and a safe build-up option without vacating the back line too aggressively.
Defensive Midfielder (Defend) holds position in front of the centre-backs, protects the space left by the two eights and gives the counter-press a stable rest-defence anchor.
Deep-Lying Playmaker (Support) receives from the defensive unit and progresses the ball through passing and decision-making.
Central Midfielder (Support) connects the holder and playmaker to the front three, preserving the passing and creativity needed for patient chance creation without adding another attack duty.
Inside forward cuts in from the left to shoot and attack the box.
Winger stays wide and delivers, giving width on the right.

Pressing Forward (Attack) leads the counter-press while supplying runs beyond the defence. Advanced Forward is an alternative when pace and movement offer a stronger depth threat, at the cost of pressing support. Poacher is an alternative for movement and finishing, with a further reduction in counter-pressing support.

description: A positive 4-3-3 built around a genuine holding midfielder, two complementary eights and three forwards who provide both width and penetration.
whyGood: It gives strong pitch coverage and multiple progression routes while preserving a real defensive anchor behind the two central midfielders. The front three can counter aggressively without requiring the DM to abandon the space in front of the centre-backs.
whyThisShape: The DM holds position while the DLP and CM provide two different connections through midfield. Shorter passing and playing out of defence use that triangle to progress securely; once possession is regained, Counter lets the inside forward, winger and striker attack before the opposition resets. The pressing forward leads pressure after losses while the holder protects the centre and both eights retain their connective roles. Work Ball Into Box favours patient chance creation, while the higher engagement line and counter-press keep the side proactive without requiring a high defensive line. An advanced forward or poacher can offer a different scoring profile, but contributes less to that counter-press.
whenToUse: As an all-round positive system when you have a reliable holding midfielder, two competent passers ahead of him, complementary wide threats and a hard-working striker who can lead the counter-press.
whenNotToUse: When the DM lacks positional discipline, the defenders are too uncomfortable to support short build-up, or the wide forwards lack the movement and pace to turn possession into penetration.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

keyRequirements: A positionally disciplined holding midfielder who protects the centre-backs rather than chasing the ball
A DLP with enough passing, touch, vision and decisions to progress shorter build-up
A supporting central midfielder who connects play reliably and complements the deep playmaker
An inside forward and winger with enough acceleration and movement to turn possession into penetration, and enough work rate and stamina to sustain the counter-press
A pressing forward with the work rate, stamina and movement to lead the counter-press and threaten space behind
Defenders and full-backs comfortable enough on the ball to make Play Out Of Defence worthwhile
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
